title: A capitalised status
prompt: Statuses in `orders` are always lowercase. This program looks for `Paid` with a capital P. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

paid = orders.filter(F.col("status") == "Paid")
print(paid.count())
print(paid.first())
print(paid.take(2))
print(orders.limit(0).count())
hints: Text comparison is exact: `"Paid"` and `"paid"` are different.
When no row matches, there is no first row. What does Python use for "nothing"?
`take` always returns a list, even when it has nothing to put in it.
explanation: No status is exactly `Paid`, so the filter keeps no rows and `count()` is 0. With no rows, `first()` returns `None` and `take(2)` returns an empty list, `[]`; neither raises an error. `limit(0)` keeps no rows at all.
